newsitem.title: USA: Cuban flotilla leader says U.S. will arrest him.
newsitem.headline: Cuban flotilla leader says U.S. will arrest him.

text.p: The leader of an exile protest flotilla planning to sail toward Cuba said on Saturday the U.S. government plans to arrest him as soon as the first boat pulls away from a U.S. dock on Sunday.

Ramon Saul Sanchez, head of the Cuban exile group Democracy Movement, said in a news release that bargaining had quickened in recent weeks between his group and U.S. officials and that he had been told by telephone he would be detained.
"He's expecting to be arrested but the flotilla will go on," said Felipe Rojas, a spokesman for Democracy Movement.
The flotilla of 30 to 40 boats scheduled to leave Key West, Florida, early on Sunday is marking the anniversary of the drowning of 41 boat people fleeing the Communist-ruled island three years ago.

The organisers said the boats would stay in international waters but Sanchez has said he intended to pilot a small boat into Cuba's territorial waters to the site eight miles (13 km) north of Havana where the 41 people died.

The United States has urged Cuba's government to act prudently towards the flotilla, the latest confrontation between Miami's Cubans and the Castro government. The Cuba government regards the flotillas as provocations.
